text: Installation On this page Environment requirements Clone the repository Preview installation steps Install Run the tests Optional physical backends Use install.sh to install Hydro-CPS-Sim and its dependencies. The installer configures system packages, a Conda environment, the OpenPLC command-line runtime, ns-3 and DHALSIM-epynet. Environment requirements Item Requirement Operating system Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04, x86_64 Python Python 3.10 in the Conda environment Environment manager Conda Privileges sudo is needed for installation and networking Internet Required for packages and source repositories Main dependencies OpenPLC command-line runtime, ns-3, DHALSIM-epynet Important: The installer builds the OpenPLC command-line runtime, not the full web management service. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/WandeF/hydro-cps-sim.git cd hydro-cps-sim Preview installation steps bash install.sh --dry-run Install Run the installer: bash install.sh conda activate hydro-cps Building ns-3 and OpenPLC may take some time. The default environment is named hydro-cps ; see bash install.sh --help for --env , --jobs , and --parent options. Run the tests The installer checks EPANET library loading and runs the Python test suite. You can also run the tests manually: python -m unittest discover -s tests After installation, follow Quick Start to run the C-Town example. The installer rewrites five top-level path keys in every C-Town YAML and saves changed originals under output/install-backups/ . Update the paths when moving to another machine or dependency directory. Optional physical backends Water keeps its EPANET environment. Install requirements-power.txt for pandapower and optionally requirements-power-plots.txt for figures. The thermal backend needs the project Python/PyYAML environment without EPANET or pandapower. Point PYTHON_BIN to the selected environment; full loops still require OpenPLC/ns-3. See Extended Experiments .

title: Quick Start
description: After installation, run your first closed-loop simulation with the C-Town example.
text: Quick Start On this page Run a simulation Select a configuration Outputs After installation, run your first closed-loop simulation with the C-Town example. Each run clears runtime/ , reports/ , st/ , and plcs/ under the configured output directory. Copy results to a separate directory before the next experiment. Start as a normal user; the script requests sudo when needed. Run a simulation cd hydro-cps-sim conda activate hydro-cps bash scripts/run_all.sh --logic-wait 0.3 Use --iterations to set the run length. This example runs 10 iterations: bash scripts/run_all.sh --iterations 10 --logic-wait 0.3 This command limits the simulation to 10 iterations to check startup and result export. Select a configuration bash scripts/run_all.sh --config examples/c_town/config.yaml Option Purpose --config PATH YAML configuration file --iterations N Number of iterations --logic-wait SECONDS Wait after SCADA downlink before reading control outputs --poll-interval SECONDS Marker polling interval --scada-modbus-workers N Concurrent SCADA Modbus workers Run bash scripts/run_all.sh --help for the definitive interface. Outputs Results are exported to reports/csv under output_path . Logs and stage timings are saved in logs/ and timing/ . At completion, the script prints: [DONE] Results: <output_path>/reports/csv Here, <output_path> is the output directory set in the configuration. Continue with experiments and configuration .

title: Experiments
description: Hydro-CPS-Sim provides MITM, DoS and PLC logic injection attacks. You can select targets and active windows to explore how attacks affect sensor
text: Security Experiments On this page Attack types Example configurations Running an experiment Reading the results Extended experiments Hydro-CPS-Sim provides MITM, DoS and PLC logic injection attacks. You can select targets and active windows to explore how attacks affect sensor data, PLC outputs and the water network. Attack types MITM, DoS and PLC logic injection entry points in the closed loop. MITM data manipulation MITM modifies Modbus data exchanged between SCADA and PLCs. For example, changing T7 measurements sent to PLC4 changes the controller input and can affect the on/off decision for PU10. DoS communication interference DoS uses UDP traffic to occupy network links and interfere with normal Modbus communication. After a timeout, SCADA may retain an earlier observation. Compare communication state, measurement updates and actuator actions to explore the effect of stale data on control. PLC logic injection Logic injection changes PLC rules, such as a pump-off threshold. OpenPLC executes the modified rules, and resulting pump or valve actions feed back into the hydraulic model. Example configurations The current version provides the following example configurations. Attack windows are measured in control iterations. Configuration Target or purpose Attack iterations config.yaml Baseline — config_mitm_plc4.yaml PLC4 downlink 20–40 config_mitm_plc9.yaml PLC8 T7 response 20–40 config_mitm_composite_plc7_plc9.yaml PLC6 T5 + PLC8 T7 20–40 / 30–50 config_dos_plc2_single.yaml PLC2, single attack endpoint 5–90 config_dos_plc2_three_bots.yaml PLC2, three attack endpoints 5–90 config_openplc_logic_plc4.yaml T7 threshold for PU10 at PLC4 20–90 Each configuration includes its network, control and attack settings. Start with an example and adjust the target, attack parameters and active window. Running an experiment Run an attack-free baseline first: bash scripts/run_all.sh --config examples/c_town/config.yaml Save the baseline output, then select an attack configuration: bash scripts/run_all.sh --config examples/c_town/config_mitm_plc4.yaml --logic-wait 0.3 Each run updates the output directory. Copy results you want to compare to a separate directory before starting the next experiment. Reading the results Results are saved under output_path in reports/csv/ . File Contents physics.csv Hydraulic states, including levels and pressures actuator_state.csv Pump and valve states scada_observed_long.csv , scada_observed_wide.csv , scada_observed_key.csv SCADA observations attack_schedule.csv , attack_events.csv Attack scheduling and events scada_timeout_events.csv Communication timeouts cycle_timing.csv Timing of closed-loop stages When comparing an attack run with its baseline, start with input changes, then inspect PLC outputs and hydraulic states. A timeout need not change an actuator action, and an input change may trigger a control rule in a later iteration. You can compare levels and pressures using RMSE, mean absolute deviation or peak absolute deviation. Use sim_time from the hydraulic records when plotting against physical time. See Configuration for network and control settings. Extended experiments For power, thermal or custom physical models, see Extended Experiments and UPSI Configuration .

title: Configuration
description: Hydro-CPS-Sim uses YAML files to configure the water network, controllers, communication and attacks. Copy an example, change the settings you ne
text: Configuration On this page File structure Paths and runtime Hydraulic time and initial conditions EPANET options PLCs and measurements Control rules Network and attacks Outputs Hydro-CPS-Sim uses YAML files to configure the water network, controllers, communication and attacks. Copy an example, change the settings you need and run it with --config . This page introduces the original examples/c_town/config.yaml water scene. To connect another physical simulator, see UPSI Configuration under Extended Experiments. File structure Section Purpose Model and component paths INP, OpenPLC, ns-3 and output directories iterations, time Run limit and hydraulic step initial_tank_values, actuators Initial tank levels and pump/valve states physics EPANET control and stepping options plcs Sensors, actuators and control rules network Communication nodes, links and addresses attacks Attack settings and active windows The following fragment shows the main fields. Copy the complete C-Town example for its PLC list and network topology. root_path: /path/to/workspace inp_file: ctown_map.inp output_path: output/baseline openplc_path: ../../../OpenPLC_v3 ns3_path: ../../../ns-3-dev-git iterations: 100 initial_tank_values: T1: '3' T2: '.5' actuators: - {name: PU1, initial_state: closed} - {name: PU2, initial_state: open} physics: inp_controls: strip step_order: next-run init_flag: 0 time: - duration: [EN_DURATION, 86400] - hydraulic_timestep: [EN_HYDSTEP, 300] Paths and runtime Field Meaning root_path Installation workspace inp_file EPANET model with pipes, equipment and demand patterns output_path This experiment's output directory openplc_path OpenPLC root ns3_path ns-3 root iterations Run limit, 100 in the example; override with --iterations network_topology_type complex label in examples; network contains the actual connections Relative paths normally start beside the YAML file. Check paths when moving a scene, and give experiments separate output directories. The retained noise_scale/log_level fields are not used as generic noise or logging controls by the current runner. Hydraulic time and initial conditions Each time entry contains an EPANET parameter name and a value. hydraulic_timestep: [EN_HYDSTEP, 300] sets the nominal step to 300 s. The example retains duration; the current runner configures the hydraulic horizon from step and iteration count. initial_tank_values assigns initial levels by tank name in INP units. C-Town uses T1–T7. Actuator names must match pump/valve links. Actuator field Meaning name Pump/valve name, such as PU1 or V2 initial_state open or closed; open enables the link and closed disables it Equipment without an automatic rule holds its initial state unless another experiment control changes it. Use hydraulic sim_time for physical-time plots and iteration to find the corresponding control record. EPANET options Field under physics Default Meaning inp_controls strip Remove runtime INP CONTROLS/RULES for external OpenPLC control; keep retains them step_order next-run Native stepping order: next-run or run-next init_flag 0 Hydraulic initialization flag also_set_setting false Also write the native link setting when controlling it These fields can also be nested under physics.epynet; that subsection takes precedence when present. Usually keep the defaults while changing models, thresholds or attacks. PLCs and measurements plcs assigns sensors and outputs. One PLC owns each measurement; SCADA forwards it to other controllers when required. Field Meaning name PLC identifier matching its network endpoint sensors Locally measured tags actuators Locally controlled pumps/valves controls Ordered control rules Tank names such as T1 mean level, junction names such as J285 mean pressure, and tags ending in F such as PU1F mean link flow. Units follow INP. For example, PLC2 measures T1 and PLC1 uses it to control PU1: plcs: - name: PLC1 sensors: [PU1F] actuators: [PU1] controls: - {dependant: T1, actuator: PU1, type: below, value: 4.0, action: open} - {dependant: T1, actuator: PU1, type: above, value: 6.3, action: closed} - name: PLC2 sensors: [T1] actuators: [] controls: [] Combine this fragment with actuator initial values and a full network. scada.name identifies SCADA; namespaces and addresses belong to network endpoints/LANs. Control rules Field Meaning dependant Measurement used by the rule actuator Controlled pump/valve type below or above the threshold value Threshold in the measurement's units action open or closed when the condition holds The example opens PU1 below 4.0 and closes it above 6.3. Between the thresholds it holds state. Comparisons are strict; equality does not trigger. Later assignments can override earlier ones when several conditions hold, so avoid conflicting rules. Network and attacks See Network Configuration . Match PLC, SCADA and attacker names across endpoints, LAN addresses and targets. Use attacks.enabled and attacks.scenarios to select attacks, targets and iteration windows. See Attack Configuration and Experiments . Outputs Results go to output_path: physics.csv, actuator_state.csv, SCADA observations and attack events. Optional reporting.key_variables selects key columns such as PLC2.PLC2_T1; otherwise water defaults apply. bash scripts/run_all.sh --config examples/c_town/config.yaml --iterations 100 --logic-wait 0.3 logic-wait is wall-clock PLC scan waiting, separate from the hydraulic step. For power, thermal or another solver, continue with Extended Experiments .

title: Network Configuration
description: The network section describes communication topology separately from the INP or electrical model. PLC, SCADA and attacker endpoint names, namespa
text: Network Configuration On this page Top-level network fields Nodes and endpoints Backbone links LANs and addresses Descriptive fields Checking a changed network The network section describes communication topology separately from the INP or electrical model. PLC, SCADA and attacker endpoint names, namespaces, IPs and access paths must agree. Top-level network fields Field Meaning backend Use ns3 topology_name Topology identifier; generated program naming follows the build workflow scheduler realtime enables RealtimeSimulatorImpl for real process traffic routing global populates routing tables pcap BOOL, false by default; enables link captures ascii_trace Reserved field; use pcap for packet capture nodes routers, switches and endpoints lists backbone_links Point-to-point backbone links lans Router/bridge/endpoint LANs taps Descriptive endpoint access list; active generation reads endpoint tap/tap_mode applications Expected communication; SCADA and PLC processes produce Modbus traffic attack_points Attack paths; set targets and parameters under attacks Nodes and endpoints Field Meaning nodes.routers[].name Unique router name nodes.switches[].name Bridge-switch name nodes.endpoints[].name PLC1, scada, mitm etc. role Router/switch metadata or endpoint plc/scada/attacker role, also used by attack lookup endpoints[].namespace Linux network namespace endpoints[].tap TAP name used by TapBridge endpoints[].tap_mode use_bridge by default or use_local; effective ns-3 endpoint mode Linux interface names have length constraints; generated veth names may be shortened. Keep namespace, TAP and IP assignments unique. network: backend: ns3 scheduler: realtime routing: global pcap: false nodes: routers: [{name: r1}] switches: [{name: s1}] endpoints: - {name: PLC1, role: plc, namespace: ns-demo-plc1, tap: tap-demo-plc1, tap_mode: use_bridge} This is a fragment; a complete scene also needs SCADA and connected backbone/LAN definitions. Backbone links Field in backbone_links[] Meaning name Unique link name type point_to_point metadata; the current list is built using PointToPointHelper rather than arbitrary type dispatch endpoints Exactly two declared nodes subnet CIDR network data_rate ns-3 rate string such as 100Mbps delay Nonnegative ns/us/ms/s string, such as 2ms mtu Bytes, commonly 1500 interfaces.NODE.ip Exact CIDR interface address interfaces.NODE.ifname Example label; ns-3 uses device objects, and Linux endpoint veth names are generated backbone_links: - name: r0-r1 type: point_to_point endpoints: [r0, r1] subnet: 10.0.1.0/24 data_rate: 100Mbps delay: 2ms mtu: 1500 interfaces: r0: {ip: 10.0.1.1/24} r1: {ip: 10.0.1.2/24} LANs and addresses Each CSMA/bridge LAN requires one router, one bridge switch and at least one endpoint. Field in lans[] Meaning name / type LAN name and csma label; current construction uses CSMA/Bridge members Declared nodes in the LAN subnet / data_rate / delay / mtu Network, shared-medium rate, delay and MTU interfaces.ROUTER.ip Router/gateway address interfaces.ENDPOINT.ip Endpoint CIDR address; runtime extracts PLC IPs here interfaces.ENDPOINT.gateway Namespace default route interfaces.NODE.ifname Descriptive label, not an actual generated-veth-name override lans: - name: plc1_lan type: csma members: [r1, s1, PLC1] subnet: 192.168.1.0/24 data_rate: 100Mbps delay: 100us mtu: 1500 interfaces: r1: {ip: 192.168.1.254/24} PLC1: {ip: 192.168.1.1/24, gateway: 192.168.1.254} Descriptive fields taps[] commonly contains endpoint, tap_name, mode and host_namespace. Keep it consistent, but actual endpoint mode follows nodes.endpoints[].tap_mode. applications[] contains name, src, dst, protocol and dst_port. attack_points[] contains name, type and targets. Metadata does not replace real endpoints, applications or attacks. Checking a changed network Match node names across members, interfaces and attacks. Keep addresses/gateways in their subnet and avoid overlapping link/LAN subnets. Add a real endpoint and LAN address for every attacker. The current generator supports bandwidth and delay as listed; there is no generic packet_loss YAML switch or automatic application traffic from applications. Additional ns-3 error models require generator implementation and inspection of generated C++. Use python -m src.run.config_info --config ... to inspect parsed settings. The build produces ns-3 C++ and Linux setup scripts. Continue with Configuration and Attacks .

title: Attack Configuration
description: Use attacks to configure MITM, UDP DoS or PLC logic injection. Choose the target, adjust attack parameters and set the active iterations.
text: Attack Configuration On this page Switches and windows Modbus MITM fields UDP DoS fields PLC logic injection Read the results Use attacks to configure MITM, UDP DoS or PLC logic injection. Choose the target, adjust attack parameters and set the active iterations. Switches and windows Field Meaning attacks.enabled Master BOOL, false by default attacks.scenarios List of independently scheduled scenarios scenarios[].name Unique process/event identifier enabled Per-scenario BOOL, true by default type modbus_mitm / udp_dos / openplc_logic_injection trigger.type Prefer iteration_window; iteration/round/round_window aliases exist trigger.start_iteration Inclusive first cycle, default 0 trigger.end_iteration Inclusive last cycle; omitted means no end limit Legacy schedule, start_round/end_round and start/end aliases remain readable. Use explicit trigger/iteration fields in new scenes. Without an iteration trigger, startup/stop defaults apply. Trigger windows use controller iterations. Rule window and traffic start_after_sec use wall-clock seconds after process startup. Both differ from physical sim_time. Modbus MITM fields Field Meaning attacker.endpoint Existing attacker node attacker.namespace / ip Descriptive identity; MITM resolves actual identity from endpoint/LAN rather than overriding it here intercept.source Usually scada; actual launcher resolves the SCADA namespace rather than selecting arbitrary clients here intercept.targets Target PLC list intercept.protocol Descriptive modbus_tcp label; current execution uses Modbus TCP intercept.port Original target port, default 502 intercept.listen_port_base Per-target listening base, fallback 15020; examples 15030 intercept.listen_ports.PLC Optional explicit per-target listen port intercept.redirect Execution is fixed to iptables_output_dnat, not dynamically switched by this label rules[].name Rule name; generated rule_N if omitted rules[].target Target PLC filter rules[].variable Actual generated REAL %MD variable on the target rules[].direction response by default or request rules[].function_codes Supported 3/4/16 list or integer; response defaults 3/4, request 16 rules[].operation set/replace, add/offset/bias or multiply/scale rules[].value Numeric replacement/offset/factor, default 0, using logical register units rules[].window.start_after_sec Delay from proxy startup, default 0 rules[].window.duration_sec Optional duration limit rules[].max_events Optional maximum matches per rule attacks: enabled: true scenarios: - name: ctown_t7_bias enabled: true type: modbus_mitm trigger: {type: iteration_window, start_iteration: 20, end_iteration: 40} attacker: {endpoint: mitm, namespace: ns-attacker, ip: 192.168.4.100} intercept: source: scada targets: [PLC4] protocol: modbus_tcp port: 502 listen_port_base: 15030 redirect: iptables_output_dnat rules: - name: tank_level_downlink target: PLC4 variable: PLC8_T7 direction: request function_codes: [16] operation: set value: 5.2 window: {start_after_sec: 0.0} This C-Town fragment sets the T7 level forwarded to PLC4 to 5.2. Change names, addresses and register variables together for another target. For a transparent comparison, use add with value 0. UDP DoS fields Field Meaning attacker.endpoint / namespace / ip Actual sender identity target.endpoint / namespace / ip Existing target identity target.protocol udp target.port UDP destination, default 502; distinct from same-number TCP Modbus traffic.mode cbr only, default cbr traffic.rate Rate string, default 500kbps; examples 120Mbps traffic.packet_size Payload bytes, default 512; examples 1400 traffic.start_after_sec Delay from attack-process startup, default 0 type: udp_dos trigger: {type: iteration_window, start_iteration: 5, end_iteration: 90} attacker: {endpoint: ns_bot1, namespace: ns-bot1, ip: 192.168.255.201} target: {endpoint: PLC2, namespace: ns-plc2, ip: 192.168.2.1, protocol: udp, port: 502} traffic: {mode: cbr, rate: 120Mbps, packet_size: 1400, start_after_sec: 0.0} This is a water-scene entry fragment; examples/c_town/config_dos_plc2_single.yaml contains the topology. Multiple senders use multiple entries/endpoints. Effects depend on actual bottlenecks, timeout/cache behavior and control thresholds. PLC logic injection The target must be an existing PLC and its namespace must match the endpoint. Field Meaning target.endpoint / namespace Actual PLC target injection.mode threshold_shift / invert_condition / force_actuator injection.restore_on_stop true by default; restore original program/runtime at window end injection.rule.actuator Rule actuator for threshold_shift/invert_condition injection.rule.dependant Rule observation injection.rule.type below/above rule match injection.rule.original_value Original threshold for threshold_shift matching injection.rule.injected_value Replacement threshold injection.rule.value invert_condition match threshold, falling back to original_value injection.actuator force_actuator output injection.state Forced BOOL/compatible state; value alias exists type: openplc_logic_injection target: {endpoint: PLC4, namespace: ns-plc4} injection: mode: threshold_shift rule: {actuator: PU10, dependant: T7, type: above, original_value: 4.8, injected_value: 999.0} restore_on_stop: true The path changes, compiles and restarts the real OpenPLC program. It does not substitute physical outputs. If matching fails, inspect ownership, thresholds and generated ST. Read the results Use attack_schedule.csv and attack_events.csv to see when attacks ran and what data changed. Compare SCADA observations, PLC outputs and hydraulic states. Communication timeouts appear in scada_timeout_events.csv. A client-confirmed MITM write can differ from the value received by the target PLC; inspect proxy records and register readback together. Data-quality settings for extended scenes are in UPSI Configuration . See Experiments , Configuration and Network Configuration .

title: Extension Overview
description: Hydro-CPS-Sim can connect power systems, thermal systems and custom physical models as well as C-Town. UPSI gives these models a common interface
text: Extended Experiments On this page Add a physical model What you can customize Run your experiment Hydro-CPS-Sim can connect power systems, thermal systems and custom physical models as well as C-Town. UPSI gives these models a common interface while PLCs, SCADA, networking and attacks follow the same workflow. Add a physical model Start with an example or write an adapter for another solver: Learn about UPSI : exchange measurements and control inputs. Write an adapter : initialize, step and read results. Configure UPSI : select the backend and connect variables, units and time. Run power and thermal examples : try complete scenes. What you can customize Goal Change Use another water network INP and inp_file; see Configuration Use another physical model physics.backend and physics.model.path Select other measurements physics.signals.observations Change commands or units physics.signals.commands and signal mappings Adjust control thresholds plcs.controls Change network or attacks network and attacks Add a simulator Implement an adapter and register it in physics.plugins Run your experiment Check model initial values and units, then run an attack-free scene. Add transparent-proxy and attack configurations when you want to compare attack behavior with the baseline. Each scene currently selects one physical backend. The model calculates system states; the platform passes them to controllers and returns the resulting commands.

title: UPSI Principles & Interface
description: UPSI (Unified Physical Simulation Interface) connects physical simulators to Hydro-CPS-Sim. Use EPANET for water, pandapower for power systems, o
text: UPSI Principles & Interface On this page Connect a physical model Follow one control cycle Adapter methods Variables and units Time and stepping Measurement status Plugins Further reading UPSI (Unified Physical Simulation Interface) connects physical simulators to Hydro-CPS-Sim. Use EPANET for water, pandapower for power systems, or add a model of your own. Connect a physical model A model supplies measurements and accepts controller outputs. A water network supplies levels, pressures and flows and accepts pump/valve commands. A thermal box supplies temperature and accepts a heater command. Their equations differ, but their role in the loop is the same. UPSI provides methods to describe variables, initialize, step and finish. An adapter calls the solver while the platform keeps the same PLC, SCADA and network workflow. UPSI connects physical simulators to the existing loop. Follow one control cycle The model produces measurements. PLCs receive them, SCADA forwards remote dependencies, and PLC rules produce commands. The platform returns those commands to the model to calculate its next state. measurements → PLC / SCADA → commands → physical model → new measurements The adapter uses native model variables; scenes use logical sensor/actuator names. SignalMapper connects them and applies unit conversions. Changing the model mainly changes the adapter and scene settings. Adapter methods Inherit PhysicsBackend and implement: Method Purpose describe() List readable/writable variables, types, units and stepping behavior initialize() Load the model, apply initial inputs and return its initial state advance(until_s, inputs) Apply inputs, advance and return the result close() Release model resources BackendConfig supplies paths, model settings, working directory, interval and initial inputs. SignalSpec describes variables; StepResult contains time, outputs, applied inputs and status. Repeated initialize calls should not restart the model. Close should work after normal completion or partial initialization. See Add a Physical Simulator . Variables and units Logical name Native example Measurement/input T1 node.T1.level Tank level V_BUS02 res_bus.BUS_02.vm_pu Bus2 voltage P_GRID metrics.total.p_grid_mw Grid active power TEMPERATURE box.temperature Box temperature HEATER heater.enabled Heater enable Ports have input/output direction and float/int/bool/str type. The existing PLC transport uses float observations and BOOL commands. Other types can use standalone model calls and need suitable bindings for PLC transport. Floats use logical = native*scale+offset; commands use the inverse. MW→kW uses scale 1000, degC→K offset 273.15. BOOL mappings may invert polarity. Specify units and conversion coefficients. Converting pu to volts also needs the model's base voltage; water-column pressure needs density and gravity. See UPSI Configuration . Time and stepping The platform requests until_s and the model returns actual time_s. Target backends reach the target; event_step backends may return at an internal event before continuing with another step. EPANET can advance through hydraulic events, pandapower solves the current AC operating point, and the thermal model integrates temperature. Returning actual time lets these methods use the same loop. Controller iteration, physical seconds and process duration are recorded separately. Use sim_time for physical curves and iteration to find matching communication/control records. Measurement status Results may include source time, quality, validity and freshness. A disconnected bus can have zero voltage marked unsupplied. Cached measurements after a network timeout retain their original source time. quality_policy selects pass-through, hold-last, skip or stop behavior at the control boundary. The physical record keeps the model's calculated result. Adapters should return complete valid outputs and raise an error when solving fails; the platform checks and records the result before continuing. Plugins EPANET and pandapower are built in. Register an independent module or installed package using physics.plugins. A scene selects one backend. Plugin selection, signal mappings and control rules are separate settings. Adding a model usually needs no scheduler, Modbus or attack-code changes. Try the thermal example , then follow the adapter tutorial . Further reading UPSI is the project's Python interface. These documents introduce related simulation, configuration and communication methods: Document Topic FMI 3.0.2 Lifecycle, variables, units and co-simulation stepping mosaik API Connecting different simulators to one experiment Python entry points Discovering installed plugins YAML / PyYAML Scene syntax and parsing Modbus Registers, coils and function codes UPSI adapters implement this project's API. An FMU adapter would additionally handle FMI calls/capabilities; simultaneous model coupling also needs inter-model exchange and time coordination.

title: Add a Physical Simulator
description: Wrap the solver as a PhysicsBackend , describe native ports and register it in the scene. Keep the adapter beside an example or in a separate Pyt
text: Add a Physical Simulator On this page Model and port design Implement the lifecycle Register the plugin Connect logical signals and PLCs Run the adapter Run the real loop Troubleshooting Wrap the solver as a PhysicsBackend , describe native ports and register it in the scene. Keep the adapter beside an example or in a separate Python package. Model and port design Identify model files, initial conditions, writable inputs, readable outputs, engineering units, physical-time API and failure states. The thermal example declares: Port Direction Type Unit box.temperature output float degC box.heater_power output float W heater.enabled input bool 1 EPANET uses node/link ports; pandapower uses result table, alias and column ports. Independent plugins can choose stable domain-specific names. Implement the lifecycle examples/thermal_box/adapter.py is a complete analytical solver adapter. A new class has this structure; the initialization and solve methods must be connected to a real solver: from src.physics.base import PhysicsBackend from src.physics.types import SignalSpec, StepResult class PlantBackend(PhysicsBackend): def __init__(self, config): self.config = config def describe(self): return {'signals': { 'plant.measurement': SignalSpec('plant.measurement', 'output', 'float', 'K'), 'plant.enabled': SignalSpec('plant.enabled', 'input', 'bool', '1'), }, 'timing': 'target', 'model_kind': 'your_physical_model'} def initialize(self): raise NotImplementedError('Connect the real solver initialization') def advance(self, until_s, inputs): raise NotImplementedError('Connect the real solver step') def close(self): pass This template produces no simulated results. Acquire solver resources in initialize, apply config.initial_inputs , and return StepResult(actual_time_s, outputs, applied_inputs, diagnostics=...) . Repeated initialization must not reset the model. Close safely after partial initialization and repeated calls. Check input types, convergence, finite outputs and actual reached time. Do not relabel cached values as newly solved observations. Declare event_step for internal-event early returns, or target for reaching each request. Register the plugin physics: backend: my_plant plugins: my_plant: factory: my_package.adapter:PlantBackend # dependency: my_solver_package An installed package can instead declare: [project.entry-points."hydro_cps.physics"] my_plant = "my_package.adapter:PlantBackend" Select it with entry_point: my_plant instead of factory. Exactly one source is required. Install the package into the Python used by PYTHON_BIN. Built-in names and aliases cannot be replaced. Connect logical signals and PLCs Merge this physical/control fragment into a scene containing complete network and runtime paths: schema_version: 2 physics: backend: my_plant plugins: my_plant: {factory: 'my_package.adapter:PlantBackend'} model: {path: model.yaml} timing: {mode: fixed_step, step_seconds: 1.0} signals: observations: TEMPERATURE: {port: plant.measurement, dtype: float, unit: K} commands: HEATER: {port: plant.enabled, dtype: bool, unit: '1'} actuators: - {name: HEATER, initial_state: false} plcs: - name: PLC1 sensors: [TEMPERATURE] actuators: [HEATER] controls: - {dependant: TEMPERATURE, actuator: HEATER, type: below, value: 293.15, action: true} - {dependant: TEMPERATURE, actuator: HEATER, type: above, value: 295.15, action: false} Ports, types and units must match describe. Remote dependencies follow sensor ownership and are forwarded by SCADA; adapters need no Modbus code. Run the adapter python -m src.physics.contract --config examples/thermal_box/config.yaml Replace the scene path for a new backend. The checker actually initializes and advances three times, validates complete data, applied inputs and physical time, and attempts cleanup. Missing declared optional dependencies are skipped; loading/model/solve errors fail. Standalone applications can pass registry = configure_plugins(raw) into BackendConfig.registry , create the backend with create_backend(name, config) and reuse exercise_backend(backend, initial_inputs, step_seconds) . Run the real loop PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python)" bash scripts/run_all.sh \ --config examples/thermal_box/config.yaml --logic-wait 0.3 Verify the existing example first, then substitute the new scene. A full run needs real OpenPLC, ns-3 and namespace privileges; the standalone contract check does not. Inspect physical_state/signals CSV, actual PLC coils, raw SCADA data and signal_quality. Confirm command k is applied in the next returned physical snapshot. Cover known trajectories, repeated initialize/close, unit/type errors, failed solves, incorrect time/timestamps and cleanup. Troubleshooting Symptom Check Plugin not found Importable package/module, same Python environment, factory or entry-point name Port/direction error Describe metadata versus scene mappings Unit error Explicit scale/offset and compatible dimensions Missing inputs Complete unique native-input mappings and initial commands Stalled/backward time Actual solver time and internal-event progress New data after failed solve Raise an error and use session-controlled publication Native concurrency issue Registry isolation does not make a solver thread-safe

title: UPSI Configuration
description: Select a physical backend, connect its signals and choose a sampling interval to use another physical model. This page introduces the UPSI additi
text: UPSI Configuration On this page Write the configuration Scene structure Reuse an existing scene Common physics fields Signal mapping fields Configure the controller Quality policy Backend-specific options Check and run Select a physical backend, connect its signals and choose a sampling interval to use another physical model. This page introduces the UPSI additions to the existing scene format. Write the configuration Keep the YAML format and add schema_version: 2 at the top level to use explicit signal configuration. Put model, signal and timing settings under physics . Use spaces, lists with - , explicit true/false and the quoted dimensionless unit '1' . PyYAML implicitly resolves unquoted on/off as booleans; quote them when strings are intended. Avoid duplicate keys and ambiguous numeric strings. See YAML and PyYAML . Use the field names listed below. Unrecognized fields may be ignored. Before running a scene, check the configuration with the commands at the end of this page. Scene structure schema_version: 2 output_path: output/baseline openplc_path: ../../../OpenPLC_v3 ns3_path: ../../../ns-3-dev-git iterations: 10 physics: {} actuators: [] plcs: [] scada: {name: scada} network: {} attacks: {enabled: false, scenarios: []} reporting: {key_variables: []} This is an outline, not a runnable empty scene. Complete starting points are examples/power_feeder/config_v2.yaml, examples/ieee33_bw/config_baseline.yaml and examples/thermal_box/config.yaml. See Network Configuration and Attack Configuration for their dictionaries. Reuse an existing scene Keep the original output/component paths, PLC rules, network and attacks. Add the following when selecting another physical model: Field Purpose schema_version: 2 Explicit physical-signal configuration physics.backend Select EPANET, pandapower or your adapter physics.model.path Physical model file physics.plugins Register an independent adapter physics.timing Physical sampling interval physics.signals Logical names mapped to native ports signals Optional top-level direction, type, unit and bounds actuators[].initial_state Initial command with its declared type, e.g. true/false quality_policy Handling unsupplied, old or missing samples initial_state Optional typed initial-output declarations; the model supplies solved initial values Common settings are described in Configuration , Network and Attacks . Common physics fields Field below physics Type / default Meaning backend v2 required string dhalsim_epynet, pandapower or a declared plugin; legacy default water, with epanet/epynet aliases model v2 required mapping Model declaration; built-ins and thermal use path; plugins may define other parameters model.path path Model file relative to scene directory plugins.NAME.factory module:Class Exactly one of factory and entry_point plugins.NAME.entry_point string Named installed hydro_cps.physics entry point plugins.NAME.dependency optional module Selected-backend import preflight init_style current / dhalsim v2 defaults current; legacy water defaults dhalsim, restricted to compatible water backends timing.mode fixed_step Current single-backend sampling schedule, distinct from internal solver stepping timing.step_seconds finite number > 0; v2 required Requested interval in seconds; EPANET needs multiples of 1 s timing.measurement_max_age_s number ≥ 0; 0 Nonzero age requires backend asynchronous-measurement capability timing.tolerance.absolute_s number ≥ 0 Default min(1e-9, step/8), at most step/4 timing.tolerance.relative number ≥ 0 Default 8× floating epsilon, at most 1e-6; final tolerance is also step-bounded signals.observations mapping Logical observations to native output ports signals.commands mapping Complete, unique logical commands to native input ports quality_policy optional mapping Same as top level; duplicate declarations must agree model_file, timestep legacy fields Model path and interval; timestep and timing.step_seconds must agree if both present sensors, actuators legacy power mappings table / element / column, with missing or invert where applicable; normalized to signals Current initialization starts from a solved time-zero snapshot. Legacy water dhalsim retains zero row 0 and configured row 1 before its historical cycle convention; a 100-round water limit therefore has 99 control cycles. Compare initialization semantics before counting snapshots. Backend describe().timing target/event_step declares solver capability, whereas scene timing.mode fixed_step selects the sampling schedule. Requests start from the last actual reached time, so internal events may shorten advancement. Signal mapping fields Applies below physics.signals.observations.NAME or commands.NAME: Field Type / default Meaning port required string Declared native port with correct direction dtype float/int/bool/str; v2 required May be supplemented by top-level signals; must match native type unit native unit String logical unit; use quoted '1' minimum, maximum optional finite numbers Numerical bounds; not valid for BOOL/string scale finite nonzero number; 1 logical = native*scale+offset; commands use inverse offset finite number; 0 Nonidentity affine transforms require float invert bool; false BOOL polarity inversion missing backend option; error Power supports zero_if_unsupplied for bus voltage only, not generic zero fill unit_context.density_kg_m3 positive number Explicit water-column pressure conversion context unit_context.gravity_m_s2 positive number Explicit gravity for that conversion calibration_reason nonempty string Reason for same-unit nonidentity calibration; recorded in schema Top-level signals.NAME accepts direction, dtype, unit, minimum and maximum. Direction and duplicate metadata must agree with mappings. Every native input needs exactly one command; duplicate command ports fail. physics: signals: observations: P_GRID_KW: {port: metrics.total.p_grid_mw, dtype: float, unit: kW, scale: 1000} commands: LOAD24_ENABLE: {port: load.LOAD_BUS24.in_service, dtype: bool, unit: '1'} MW→kW uses scale 1000; degC→K uses offset 273.15. The unit catalog separates active/reactive power and incompatible dimensions. Per-unit voltage allows identity without guessing a voltage base. See UPSI . Configure the controller Sensor ownership and threshold rules keep their original structure. Measurement names now refer to physics.signals.observations and commands to physics.signals.commands. Match each initial value to its declared type. actuators: - {name: LOAD24_ENABLE, initial_state: true} plcs: - {name: PLC1, sensors: [V_BUS02], actuators: [], controls: []} - name: PLC3 sensors: [V_BUS24, P_LOAD24] actuators: [LOAD24_ENABLE] controls: - {dependant: V_BUS02, actuator: LOAD24_ENABLE, type: below, value: 0.95, action: false} - {dependant: V_BUS02, actuator: LOAD24_ENABLE, type: above, value: 1.03, action: true} Thresholds use logical units, here pu. LOAD24_ENABLE true connects the load. Use invert in a BOOL mapping when the native command polarity differs. Quality policy quality_policy: default: pass_through overrides: unsupplied: hold_last stale: fail_fast missing: skip_write Actions are pass_through, hold_last, skip_write and fail_fast. Override conditions are good, initial, unsupplied, invalid, missing and stale. Missing/invalid takes precedence, then stale sample/transport, then source quality. Default pass-through preserves compatible finite data but does not fill unusable values with good zeros. Hold caches update only on successful writes; without history they skip. Backend-specific options EPANET See water configuration for inp_controls, step_order, init_flag and also_set_setting. Explicit ports use node.ID.level/pressure/head/demand and link.ID.flow/status/setting; commands use link.ID.status. Units follow INP. pandapower Solver options algorithm, max_iteration and tolerance_mva are passed to real runpp; omitted values use pandapower defaults, with numba=False. Unknown solver options fail. Model YAML field Meaning sn_mva Declarative network base, default 1 MVA buses[] name, vn_kv and native create_bus parameters ext_grids[] name, bus alias, vm_pu and native external-grid parameters lines[] name, from_bus/to_bus aliases, length_km, r_ohm_per_km, x_ohm_per_km, c_nf_per_km, max_i_ka and native line parameters loads[] name, bus alias, p_mw, q_mvar and native load parameters switches[] name, bus, element alias, et=l line or b bus, closed and native switch parameters load_profiles.LOAD Nonempty nonnegative scaling list indexed by iteration, holding its last value afterwards source / case Public-model whitelist: pandapower_builtin / case33bw benchmark_mode original required for public source; physical overrides rejected source_citation Public model provenance aliases.NAME table=bus and paper_bus_number; source-name-based paper mapping controlled_elements.NAME table=load, bus_number, field=in_service; exactly one load must match Public-source and manually declared models follow separate loading paths. Native parameters are documented in pandapower . Result ports are res_bus/res_line/res_load/res_ext_grid.ALIAS.COLUMN, e.g. supported vm_pu, p_mw, q_mvar, pl_mw and loading_percent columns. Derived MW ports are metrics.total.p_grid_mw/p_loss_mw/served_load_mw/unserved_load_mw. BOOL commands use switch.ALIAS.closed or load.ALIAS.in_service. Thermal box Model fields are ambient_c, initial_c, loss_per_s (s⁻¹), heater_c_per_s (°C/s), heater_w (W) and input_dtype (bool, or float for the standalone analog API). Ports are box.temperature, box.heater_power and heater.enabled. Check and run python -m src.run.config_info --config examples/power_feeder/config_v2.yaml python -m src.physics.contract --config examples/power_feeder/config_v2.yaml bash scripts/run_all.sh --config examples/power_feeder/config_v2.yaml --iterations 10 --logic-wait 0.3 config_info validates/prints configuration without a solver run. Contract actually runs the backend without networking. run_all executes the full loop. logic-wait is wall-clock PLC scan waiting, not physical sampling time. Communication timeout, synchronization and worker options belong to runner CLI settings; do not invent equivalent YAML keys. Continue with Network and Attack Configuration .

Run them directly or change the models and control rules for your own experiments. Four-bus feeder The 20 kV radial model has grid, feeder, control and flexible buses, a 0.2 MW essential load and a 0.8 MW switched load. PLC1 measures voltage and power; PLC2 receives V_CONTROL, disconnecting below 0.95 pu and reconnecting above 1.03 pu. python -m pip install -r requirements-power.txt python -m src.physics.contract --config examples/power_feeder/config_v2.yaml PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python)" bash scripts/run_power_experiments.sh python scripts/check_power_results.py Configuration in examples/power_feeder Purpose config.yaml Attack-free baseline config_mitm_transparent.yaml Same proxy/path, zero bias config_mitm.yaml −0.15 pu on SCADA→PLC2 PLC1_V_CONTROL FC16 writes, cycles 3–6 config_v2.yaml Explicit UPSI v2 baseline With these settings, the example shows transparent equality, the first actual coil deviation at cycle 3 and the first physical load-power change at 4: 0.8→0 MW. Disconnected bus voltage zero is explicitly marked unsupplied. IEEE33 benchmark examples/ieee33_bw/model.yaml loads pandapower.networks.case33bw() , preserving public source voltage, impedances, loads and five open ties. The 12.66 kV model has 33 buses, 37 lines and 3.715 MW / 2.300 MVAr demand. python scripts/ieee33_reference.py python -m src.physics.contract --config examples/ieee33_bw/config_baseline.yaml PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python)" bash scripts/run_ieee33_experiments.sh python scripts/check_ieee33_results.py PLC1 measures Bus2, PLC2 monitors remote voltages, and PLC3 controls the existing Bus24 0.420 MW / 0.200 MVAr load using forwarded Bus2 voltage. The derived MITM subtracts 0.10 pu during cycles 20–40. Metric Example result Original minimum voltage About 0.91309048 pu, Bus18 Original line loss About 202.677 kW Baseline / transparent / MITM 100 cycles each; transparent equals baseline First command / physical difference 20 / 21 Bus24 load 0.420→0 MW; bus stays energized PLC remote control, thresholds and attacks are derived platform experiments; MATPOWER case33bw supplies the benchmark network. Results are AC quasi-steady snapshots, without electromagnetic or frequency dynamics. Thermal-box plugin The independent examples/thermal_box/adapter.py solves: dT/dt = -0.1 × (T - 18) + 0.8 × HEATER heater power = 800 × HEATER W Initial temperature is 19 °C and ambient temperature 18 °C. PLC1 provides temperature/power; PLC2 heats below 20 °C, stops above 22 °C and holds in between. python -m src.physics.contract --config examples/thermal_box/config.yaml PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python)" bash scripts/run_all.sh \ --config examples/thermal_box/config.yaml --logic-wait 0.3 In the ten-cycle real loop, heating stops at command 6, cooling first appears in physical snapshot 7, and temperature at 10 s is about 20.7874 °C. The backend uses analytical integration without EPANET or pandapower.
